newsitem.title: USA: Tosco may appeal Calif. agency's citation.
newsitem.headline: Tosco may appeal Calif. agency's citation.

text.p: Tosco Corp said on Thursday it would consider an appeal after a California regulatory agency cited the company for 22 alleged safety violations over a fatal explosion at a California refinery.

The California Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA) said earlier it had cited Tosco's refining arm for 22 alleged violations of state workplace safety regulations after completing its investigation into a Jan. 21 explosion at Tosco's Avon refinery near San Francisco.
One Tosco employee was killed in the blast and 46 Tosco and contractor workers were injured, it said.
Cal/OSHA called for total penalties against the company of $277,750, which it said was the highest penalty it had levied against an oil refining company in California.
"We're very concerned about the citations and the amount of the penalty," Tosco spokesman David Kory said.
"We will discuss the proposed violations with them (Cal/OSHA) and will consider filing an appeal," he said.
Tosco has 15 working days to appeal the citiations and penalties to the Occupational Safety and Health Appeals Board in Sacramento. Suggested penalties are sometimes revised downwards on appeal.
Kory said Tosco had conducted its own comprehensive investigation after the accident and had "identified opportunities for improvement and implemented all of the recommendations."
The Contra Costa County Health Department had also conducted a thorough investigation and Tosco had implemented its recommendations, he said.

Kory said Tosco had made about $60 million in improvements to the hydrocracker unit. The hydrocracker recently resumed operating after being out of service for several months after the accident while the improvements were made.
